title: Leak Detection in Port Alder | Non-Invasive | Harbourview
description: Find hidden water leaks without tearing out walls. Acoustic and thermal leak detection for homes in Port Alder, Cedar Falls and Millbrook.
lead: A rising water bill, a warm patch on the floor, a stain that keeps spreading. We find the leak with listening gear and thermal imaging, then open the wall in one place.

sections.heading: Signs you have a hidden leak
sections.html:
Most hidden leaks announce themselves slowly. The water meter dial keeps turning with every tap closed. A section of hardwood starts to cup. You hear water running at night when nobody is using any. In older harbour-side homes with copper lines, pinhole leaks are common where the pipe passes through a damp crawlspace, and they can drip for months before anything shows upstairs.

Slab homes in the newer valley subdivisions have a different pattern: a hot-water line under the slab starts leaking and you notice a warm spot on the tile. That one needs to be found precisely, because every extra square foot of concrete we cut is time and money.

sections.heading: Tools we use
items: Meter and pressure tests to confirm there is a leak and which side of the system it's on
Acoustic ground microphones that pick up water escaping a pressurised line
Thermal imaging to trace hot-water lines through floors and walls
Moisture meters to map how far the water has spread
Tracer gas for leaks too quiet to hear

items.title: Confirm
items.text: We isolate the fixtures and pressure-test each line to narrow the search.

items.title: Locate
items.text: Listening and imaging pinpoint the spot, usually to within a hand's width.

items.title: Report
items.text: Photos and moisture readings you can send straight to your insurer.

items.title: Repair
items.text: We open the smallest area possible, repair the line and re-test before closing up.

items.a: Many policies cover the cost of finding and accessing a sudden leak, though not always the pipe repair. Our written report has what most adjusters ask for.
Most searches take one to three hours. Slab leaks and long underground service lines can take longer.
